speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) whether there is a need to review the provisions of the Misuse of Drugs Act in light of the Court of Appeal's judgment in Adili Chibuke Ejike vs Public Prosecutor; and (b) how will the presumptions in the Misuse of Drugs Act continue to function as key legal tools to battle drug trafficking within, into or through Singapore to make Singapore drug-free.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In practice, it can be difficult to prove a person's state of mind.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: It is then for the accused to give sufficient evidence to rebut the presumptions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: There is also the legal concept of "willful blindness".

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Under the law, a person will be treated as having knowledge of a fact, if it can be shown that he: (a) suspected something was amiss; (b) yet, did not verify his suspicion out of fear of legal consequences; and (c) he had reasonable means of discovering the truth.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Adili was arrested at Changi Airport in November 2011 after flying in from Nigeria.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Two packets containing close to two kg of Ice were found concealed in the inner lining of his suitcase.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Adili claimed that an acquaintance in Nigeria had told him to pass the suitcase to an unknown person in Singapore and he was given about US$5,000 for his travel expenses.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: He claimed that he does not know what the suitcase contained, why he had to deliver it, and he did not ask those questions of his acquaintance.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The one issue was whether Adili could rebut the presumption that he knew the nature of the drugs in his suitcase.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The presumption allows the Court to conclude that the accused did know.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: But if the prosecution accepts that the accused did not know of that fact, then obviously the presumption cannot be relied upon.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This legal reasoning is neither novel nor new and is not in any way different from the Government’s understanding of the law.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I have asked the Senior Parliamentary Secretary to confirm whether my understanding is still valid and correct.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: And, if it is valid and correct, that is, that the presumptions continue to be legal and muscular tools, then arising out of this decision, can the accused now claim a defence that he had no knowledge just by virtue of the drugs being well-concealed?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I certainly hope that an accused should not be able to avail himself of such a defence.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Our drug laws have been effective and remain so.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: We have presumptions under the MDA because it can be difficult to prove a person's state of mind as it is something that is intangible and cannot be seen.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The presumptions under the MDA impose a legal burden on accused persons to rebut the presumed facts on a balance of probabilities.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The presumptions were introduced precisely to address the difficulty of proving an accused person's subjective state of knowledge.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: This has been our policy intent right from the beginning.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Instead, the outcome of each case depends on a holistic assessment of all its unique facts and circumstances as well as the evidence.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Our Courts in the past have carefully scrutinised such claims to assess if they are credible such that the presumption is rebutted.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: And I am confident that they will continue to do so.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Moreover, when the presumptions apply, the accused persons bear the onus of persuading the Court that such claims are credible and should be believed.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: One point worth noting is the robustness of our criminal justice system.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: If the prosecution fails to discharge its burden of proof, an accused person will be acquitted.
